newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia and Vatican sign agreements.
newsitem.headline: Croatia and Vatican sign agreements.

text.p: Croatia and the Vatican signed three agreements on Thursday to regulate their relations and strengthen the position of the Roman Catholic Church in Croatia, the state news agency HINA reported.

With the accords, Croatia became the first country emerging from the fall of communism in Eastern Europe to establish full ties with the Vatican, said Jure Radic, head of Croatia's state commission for religion.
Radic and papal nuncio Giulio Einaudi signed accords on legal issues, cooperation in culture and education, and the presence of Roman Catholic priests in the army and police.
More than 90 percent of Croats are Roman Catholics. Pope John Paul II visited Zagreb in 1994, three years after Croatia declared independence from federal Yugoslavia.
"(The agreements) in general resolve the status of the Catholic Church in Croatia because the church and its institutions are now recognised as a legal entity," Croatian Cardinal Franjo Kuharic said.
Relations between the Croatian government and the church have been strained over the latter's demand for the return of extensive properties nationalised under Yugoslav rule.
But Kuharic said an accord straightening out economic ties between the church and Croatian state should be signed soon.
